*   **Patient Name:** Rowan Carter

*   **Reference Number:** POC-CD6AF51965-72160
*   **Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-10
*   **Denied Service:** Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)
*   **Prescribing Surgeon:** Dr. Duval, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)

To the Medical Review Director:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my scheduled arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), to be performed by Dr. Duval. The denial letter dated August 10, 2026, states that the "clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

A review of my complete clinical file demonstrates that I have not only undergone an extensive trial of conservative treatments but have far exceeded the specific threshold requirements outlined in Molina Healthcare’s medical policy. I request that you review the comprehensive clinical timeline below and reverse this denial immediately.

### Clinical History and Documented Trial of Conservative Treatment

My medical records document a persistent, 24-month history of progressive right shoulder pain that is unrelieved by rest and severely impacts my daily life. To address this, I completed a multi-modality conservative care regimen spanning several months:

1.  **Prescription Strength Anti-inflammatory Medications (NSAIDs):** I utilized prescription NSAIDs for **8 months** to manage the pain, which provided inadequate relief. 
2.  **Intraarticular Corticosteroid Injection:** On **April 21, 2026**, I received a localized corticosteroid injection in the affected shoulder. This provided only partial relief that lasted for a brief period of 3 weeks before my severe symptoms returned.
3.  **Supervised Physical Therapy:** From **May 23, 2026, to July 18, 2026** (an 8-week period), I completed **24 sessions** of highly structured, supervised physical therapy. My sessions focused specifically on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. Despite 100% compliance, my symptoms did not resolve, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

My cumulative trial of conservative care spans from approximately late 2025 through July 2026 (at least 8 months), incorporating physical therapy, oral medications, and an injection. 

### Objective Clinical Severity and Functional Impairment

Because conservative management failed to restore my shoulder joint function or relieve my pain, an MRI of my shoulder was performed on **July 6, 2026**. The MRI revealed:
*   A **full-thickness supraspinatus tendon tear measuring 1.8 cm**.
*   **Grade 2 fatty atrophy** of the supraspinatus muscle.

The presence of Grade 2 fatty atrophy is highly significant; it indicates that my chronic tear is leading to irreversible muscle degeneration. Further delaying surgical repair to undergo additional "conservative" treatment will result in permanent loss of muscle quality, rendering the tendon irreparable and leading to joint destruction.

My current functional limitations are severe: I am completely unable to lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on my affected side due to excruciating pain. On physical examination, Dr. Duval documented pain-limited range of motion and positive provocative testing on my affected side. I have no active infections, no untreated substance use, a healthy BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker, making me an excellent candidate for successful surgical intervention.

### Alignment with Molina Healthcare Medical Policy

The denial was evaluated under Molina's clinical guidelines. Molina's governing policy for this procedure is:
*   **Policy Title:** "Shoulder Arthroscopy Guidelines"
*   **Policy Number:** "MCP-404"
*   **Original Effective Date:** "2021-06-09" (Revision/Review Date: "6/29/21")

Under the clinical criteria of "MCP-404", the policy dictates:
> "This policy addresses arthroscopic procedures when performed as an elective, non-emergent technique for disease pathology that will cause progressive destruction. Please see MCG criteria for rotator cuff repair."

While "MCP-404" defers to MCG Health's proprietary guidelines for the specific clinical indications of a rotator cuff repair, "MCP-404" outlines the standard requirements for shoulder arthroscopy procedures, defining conservative therapy failure as follows:
> "Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:
> o Activity modification
> o Assistive devices (e.g., sling, splint, brace)
> o Physical therapy
> o Physician or physical therapist-supervised therapeutic home exercise program which includes flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises
> o Prescription strength anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics
> o Intraarticular corticosteroid injection(s)"

*(Note: The plan's referenced MCG Health guidelines are proprietary, and their exact text has not been quoted in this letter).*

My medical history shows I have met and exceeded these requirements:
*   **Duration:** My non-surgical management trial spanned **8 months** (from November 2025 through July 2026), easily satisfying the "at least three (3) months in duration" standard.
*   **Modalities:** I completed **three** of the listed non-surgical modalities—Physical Therapy (24 sessions over 8 weeks), "Prescription strength anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics" (taken for 8 months), and an "Intraarticular corticosteroid injection(s)" (administered on April 21, 2026).

### Conclusion

The clinical documentation submitted with my prior authorization packet clearly confirms that I have exhausted conservative treatment. My 1.8 cm full-thickness tear is accompanied by Grade 2 fatty atrophy, which will progress to permanent, irreversible disability if surgical repair is delayed any further.

I meet all the medical necessity requirements under Molina Policy "MCP-404" and the associated clinical guidelines. I strongly urge you to overturn this denial and approve the requested rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827). 

If you require any further documentation, please contact Dr. Duval's office at [Doctor's Phone Number] or me directly at [Patient Phone Number]. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Rowan Carter
[Patient Signature]
